source_text: Thomas Puls of IW Köln fears that the strikes will harm the image of Germany as a place for business. Local bosses are already fretting about a German version of the gilets jaunes protests in France in 2018, which culminated in yellow-jacketed demonstrators torching cars on the Champs-Elysées and the police stepping in with tear gas. Jochen Kopelke, head of Germany's police union, warned in an interview with Tagesspiegel, a daily, that the farmers were probably "just the start of an enormous wave of protest this year." Germany was the only big economy to shrink in 2023, and the year ended on an especially sour note, with an unexpected drop in business confidence in December. This year is shaping up to be even tougher.
input_text: Thomas Puls frá IW Köln óttast að verkföllin muni skaða mynd Þýskalands sem viðskiptastaðar. Staðbundnir yfirmenn eru þegar að hafa áhyggjur af þýskri útgáfu mótmælanna gilets jaunes í Frakklandi árið 2018, sem náðu hápunkti þegar mótmælendur í gulvöttum jakkafötum kveiktu í bílum á Champs-Elysées og lögreglan kom við með tárargas. Jochen Kopelke, formaður lögreglufélagsins í Þýskalandi, varaði í viðtali við Tagesspiegel, dagblað, að bændurnir væru líklega „bara upphaf stórbrotinnar mótmælaöldu á þessu ári.“ Þýskaland var eina stóra hagkerfið sem minnkaði árið 2023, og árið lauk sérstaklega súrt, með óvæntum minnkun í viðskiptatryggð í desember. Þetta ár verður líklega enn erfiðara.

source_text: Thomas Puls of IW Köln fears that the strikes will harm the image of Germany as a place for business. Local bosses are already fretting about a German version of the gilets jaunes protests in France in 2018, which culminated in yellow-jacketed demonstrators torching cars on the Champs-Elysées and the police stepping in with tear gas. Jochen Kopelke, head of Germany's police union, warned in an interview with Tagesspiegel, a daily, that the farmers were probably "just the start of an enormous wave of protest this year." Germany was the only big economy to shrink in 2023, and the year ended on an especially sour note, with an unexpected drop in business confidence in December. This year is shaping up to be even tougher.

Jochen Kopelke, yfirmaður lögreglusambands Þýskalands, varaði við því í viðtali við dagblaðið Tagesspiegel að bændurnir væru líklega „bara upphafið að gríðarlegri mótmælaöldu á þessu ári". source_text: In an interview with Ventures Africa, an anonymous Senior Legal Official from a leading commercial bank commented, "There are several issues concerning this matter. First, her ministry is relatively new, and her predecessor and pioneering minister, Sadiya Umar-Farouk, engaged in activities that appeared to be illegal. It might be a reflection of how they operate in the ministry. Nevertheless, paying public money into private accounts goes against public procurement rules." He added that unless she can provide a valid reason for such approval, it may not necessarily involve fraudulent intent, but it is nonetheless incorrect, and certainty is lacking.
input_text: Í viðtali við Ventures Africa, ónefndur æðsti lögfræðingur frá leiðandi viðskiptabanka sagði: „Það eru margar deilur um þessa málefni. Fyrst og fremst er ráðuneyti hennar nýtt og fyrirrennari hennar, Sadiya Umar-Farouk, sem var píónieri ráðuneytisins, tók þátt í athöfnum sem virtust ólöglegar. Það gæti verið endurtekt á því hvernig þeir starfa í ráðuneytinu. En þótt það sé svo, að greiða opinbera fjármuni í einkareikninga, er gegn opinberum kaupreglum.“ Hann bætti við að nema hún geti gefið giltan ástæðu fyrir slíku samþykki, má það ekki þýða að hún hafi verið í ósiðlegum áformum, en það er þó rangt, og vísdómur vantar.

Local bosses are already fretting about a German version of the gilets jaunes protests in France in 2018, which culminated in yellow-jacketed demonstrators torching cars on the Champs-Elysées and the police stepping in with tear gas. Jochen Kopelke, head of Germany's police union, warned in an interview with Tagesspiegel, a daily, that the farmers were probably "just the start of an enormous wave of protest this year." Germany was the only big economy to shrink in 2023, and the year ended on an especially sour note, with an unexpected drop in business confidence in December. This year is shaping up to be even tougher.
